pr.title: Turn moves into copies after copy propagation
pr.description:
Previously copy propagation presumed that there is further unspecified distinction between move operands and copy operands in assignments and propagated moves from assignments into terminators. This is inconsistent with current operational semantics.

Turn moves into copies after copy propagation to preserve existing behavior.

Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/137936.
Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/146423.

r? @cjgillot
pr.author: tmiasko

processing.reason: The historical change is not an executable value-semantics bug on current Rust/Miri; it is a MIR-transformation/specification fix. The old Replacer differed only by emitting `Operand::Move` instead of `Operand::Copy` for a unified local. That difference can only be observed when the same unified local is moved more than once. The PR's own reproducers (`moved_twice`, `moved_and_copied`) and MIR diffs show this situation arises from custom MIR, not safe Rust, and the PR comments explicitly say the move-propagation variant would require future operational semantics to explain overlapping moves in a call terminator. Under the current compiler and Miri, moves of Copy values (including `MaybeUninit<T: Copy>`) are bitwise copies, so `move _1` twice and `copy _1` twice have identical values/behavior. For non-Copy ownership types, repeated moves of one source either double-drop in both formulations or are already invalid; for `&mut` reborrows, the tests only assert textual MIR (`move _2` vs `copy _2`), not an execution result. Thus any pair whose original execution is defined cannot be made to diverge solely by this historical move-vs-copy rewrite without manufacturing an unrelated semantic change.

analysis.summary: CopyProp formerly preserved/propagated move operands for locals deemed "fully moved", which could emit `move _a` after substituting a move-derived local. This is soundness-relevant because it can move from the same unified local more than once (e.g. overlapping call operands or a reborrow later re-used). The fix removes the move/copy distinction: after copy propagation every unified place is accessed with `copy`, and any `Operand::Move` of a unified local is rewritten to `Operand::Copy`. Confirmed bug fix for rust-lang/rust#137936 and #146423.
analysis.originalLogic: CopyProp computed SSA copy equivalence classes and a `fully_moved_locals` bitset from assignments whose RHS was `Operand::Move`; it propagated class representatives into uses but deliberately left moves as moves for locals in `fully_moved`, replacing them with `copy` only otherwise. It also excluded StorageLive/StorageDead from local substitution and tracked only class heads in `storage_to_remove`. The old doc stated that locals would be replaced "either copied or moved", and that a local in the bitset could be replaced by a move while otherwise it must be replaced by a copy.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically wrong rewrite is propagating a move operand as a move of the unified source local, e.g. turning `_6 = move _4; _5 = opaque::<&mut u8>(move _6)` into `_5 = opaque::<&mut u8>(move _2)` instead of `_5 = opaque::<&mut u8>(copy _2)`. In general, the old pass could transform `move _c` into `move _a` whenever the equivalence class containing `_c` was classified as `fully_moved`, rather than always using `copy _a` after propagation. This presumes an unspecified move/copy distinction inconsistent with operational semantics and can produce multiple moves out of one unified local or overlap in a call terminator. The corrected output uses `copy _a` for every propagated place.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies after SSA/copy-equivalence analysis that contain locals connected by `_d = copy _c` / `_d = move _c` assignments and merge into `Operand::Move(place)` uses (assignments, call terminators, and custom-MIR calls). Relevant inputs include multiple uses/moves of the same source local, &mut/raw reborrows that are used again after an opaque call, and `MaybeUninit<T>` or other types where overlapping moves are questionable. A focused pair can differ only in whether a propagated move is emitted as `move` or `copy` of the source local.
analysis.trigger: A non-head local is in a CopyProp equivalence class (so `any_replacement` is true), and an `Operand::Move(place)` with `place.local` in the unified set is visited after substitution. The old logic is especially exposed when `place.local` was classified as fully moved, or when the same source local is moved/read by more than one operand (e.g. `Call(f(Move(_1), Move(_2)))` or a reborrow used after an opaque call).
preconditions: CopyProp has found at least one local whose copy-class representative differs from itself (`local != head`).
The operand is `Operand::Move(place)` and the place is not an indirect first projection (`!place.is_indirect_first_projection()`).
The place local participates in a copy class as source or destination, now recorded in `unified` for both head and non-head locals.
StorageLive/StorageDead statements for unified locals must be removed together, not left with only one counterpart nop'ed.
pitfalls: Do not preserve or emit `move _a` merely because the original assignment was a move; after propagation, use `copy _a` so a single unified local cannot be moved multiple times.
Do not treat a move from a projection as equivalent to a copy of the projection when it is indirect-first; the `is_indirect_first_projection` guard must remain.
Do not rewrite StorageLive/StorageDead locals only for class heads; both source and destination locals are unified and both storage statements must be handled consistently.
The old early return after nop'ing one storage statement is removed so the remaining statement/visitor logic is not skipped; the intent is to remove both (#107511).

Changing move propagation to copy propagation affects downstream analyses (e.g. the large_assignments lint now fires on additional moves); update UI expectations accordingly rather than assuming the lint behavior is unchanged.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `//@ test-mir-pass: CopyProp` MIR-opt test using `#![feature(custom_mir, core_intrinsics)]` and `#[custom_mir(dialect = "runtime", phase = "initial")]` to force explicit `Move` operands. Cover (1) a local copied once then moved twice in a call (`moved_and_copied`) and assert the post-pass call uses `copy _1, copy _1`; (2) two explicit moves of the same source into a call (`moved_twice`, using `MaybeUninit<T>`) and assert `copy _1, copy _1`, documenting the future operational-semantics work. Update `reborrow.remut`/`reborrow.reraw` MIR expectations from `move _2` to `copy _2`. Run/review large_assignments UI tests, which now expect additional `large_assignments` errors for inlined MIR and move-into-function cases. Do not claim execution; these are source-level MIR/diff expectations.
evidence: Previously copy propagation presumed that there is further unspecified distinction between move operands and copy operands in assignments and propagated moves from assignments into terminators.
Turn moves into copies after copy propagation to preserve existing behavior.
We want to replace all those locals by `copy _a`.
A local which is in the bitset can be replaced by `move _a`. Otherwise, it must be
replaced by `copy _a`, as we cannot move multiple times from `_a`.
// In a future we would like to propagate moves instead of copies here. The resulting program
// would have an undefined behavior due to overlap in a call terminator, so we need to change
// operational semantics to explain why the original program has undefined behavior.
// When removing storage statements, we need to remove both (#107511).
